title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Embodied Agents: On the Path to Real-World Physical Intelligence
content: Embodied artificial intelligence is moving beyond static task execution toward agents that can continuously adapt, learn, and improve through physical interaction with the world. While recent advances in large language models, vision-language models, robotic foundation models, vision-language-action models, and world models have significantly enhanced the perception, reasoning, and action capabilities of embodied agents, most existing systems remain constrained by offline training, fixed policies, and limited post-deployment adaptability. This survey investigates self-evolving embodied agents as an emerging research agenda for advancing toward real-world physical intelligence. We define self-evolution as the capability of embodied agents to accumulate experience, detect and correct errors, update memory, policies, skills, and models, and expand their capability boundaries through long-term interaction. To make the review auditable, we specify the literature scope, inclusion criteria, evidence types, and coding rules used in the comparative tables. We first clarify the conceptual foundations of self-evolving embodied agents and distinguish them from related paradigms such as test-time adaptation, online learning, continual learning, and lifelong learning. We then propose a unified closed-loop framework consisting of perception, state representation, memory, reasoning and planning, action, feedback, reflection, and evolution. Based on this framework, we review the historical progression from classical robotics and offline embodied learning to embodied foundation models, interactive adaptation, and self-evolving agents. We further summarize key mechanisms supporting self-evolution, including data and experience acquisition, memory-centric learning, world-modeldriven prediction, feedback-based reflection, policy and skill evolution, multi-agent co-evolution, and safety-aligned updating. Finally, we discuss representative tasks, benchmarks, evaluation protocols, open challenges, and future directions. This survey argues that self-evolution is a necessary but still weakly evidenced step toward embodied agents that can safely, autonomously, and continually grow in open-ended real-world environments.
